The test image shows a tomato shoot with:
- Prominent interveinal chlorosis on the upper leaf (veins stay green, tissue between turns yellow)
- Yellow-green mottled/mosaic appearance on the affected leaf
- Lower leaves appear normal green
- Some leaf distortion

This interveinal chlorosis pattern points toward Verticillium Wilt (which causes V-shaped yellowing and interveinal chlorosis) or possibly a viral mosaic. Let me check a Verticillium Wilt reference.

The Verticillium Wilt reference shows wilting/bleaching with marginal necrosis - quite different from the test image. The test image has crisp interveinal chlorosis (green veins, yellow tissue between) with a mosaic-like pattern and slight leaf distortion but no wilting. This pattern of interveinal mosaic/chlorosis without necrotic spots or wilting is most characteristic of **Cucumber Mosaic Virus**.

The lower leaves are still normal green, suggesting early/localized infection. This yellow-green mosaic with interveinal chlorosis and no necrotic spots or wilting is most consistent with Cucumber Mosaic Virus. Verticillium Wilt was ruled out as the reference showed wilting/bleaching rather than mosaic patterning."}
